strengths: The paper addresses a practical bottleneck in multimodal inference through a lightweight module between the vision encoder and projector. Reducing visual tokens from 576 to approximately 40 offers substantial potential savings while retaining the language-model backbone.

Evaluation covers six benchmarks and both 7B and 13B models. Despite aggressive compression, the fine-tuned models retain strong ScienceQA and POPE performance, demonstrating a potentially useful efficiency–accuracy tradeoff.

The ablations provide encouraging evidence: training-free PruMerge improves TextVQA over spatial sampling (54.00 versus at most 47.96 in Table 3), and adding token supplementation improves MME from 1221.6 to 1350.3 in Table 4.

The high-level pipeline is clearly illustrated, relevant models, datasets, and token-merging antecedents are cited, and the limitations section acknowledges lossy compression and restricted validation.
weaknesses: The claims of comparable performance and preserved reasoning capabilities are too broad for the results. Table 1 shows VQAv2 losses of 6.5 and 7.2 percentage points for 7B and 13B, respectively; 7B MME falls from 1510.7 to 1350.3, and 13B MMBench falls from 67.7 to 62.3. Training-free POPE drops from 85.9 to 76.2 in Table 5. These tradeoffs may still be valuable, but describing the degradation as marginal understates important task-dependent losses.

The comparisons do not establish the contribution beyond existing pruning and merging ingredients. Table 3 tests only sequential and spatial sampling; fixed-budget CLS-attention top-k selection and an established token-merging baseline are missing. A comparison using identical merging and matched average token budgets would isolate the benefit of IQR adaptivity. Accuracy-versus-budget curves and matched fine-tuning controls are also needed: the proposed main models receive an additional LoRA epoch, whereas equivalent adaptation is not reported for the comparison methods.

The efficiency evidence consists of roofline estimates for LLM prefill, rather than measured deployment performance. Table 2 does not establish end-to-end latency or peak-memory savings after accounting for vision encoding, selection/merging overhead, decoding, and batching variable token counts. Its nominal FLOPs also decrease approximately fourfold under INT4 for the unchanged architecture and token count, requiring clarification of whether these are precision-weighted operation counts. The analysis supports potential savings but does not adequately validate the practical acceleration claims.

Important algorithmic details are missing or inconsistent. Algorithm 1 excludes the selected center from its neighbor candidates and replaces it with an unnormalized attention-weighted sum, whereas the introduction describes weighted averaging that supplements retained tokens. Center inclusion and weight normalization materially affect retained information and feature scale. The neighborhood size k, attention-head aggregation, cluster-overlap handling, and LoRA hyperparameters are also unspecified, limiting reproducibility from the supplied manuscript.

The central interpretation of adaptivity is weakly supported. A few visualizations and an overall mean of 40 tokens do not establish that IQR-selected token counts track image complexity or preserve question-relevant details. Token-count distributions, sensitivity analysis, and failure cases would help validate this assumption. Both model sizes use LLaVA-1.5 at 336-pixel resolution, so the high-resolution and video applications motivating the work remain untested.
